## The 175-year frame

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

The 47-year-old Islamic Republic is not the right analytical baseline for what Iran does in 2026. The relevant baseline runs back to **1813** (Treaty of Golestan, Iran's first major territorial loss to Russia) and arguably to **1501** (Safavid imposition of Twelver Shi'ism). What looks like unprecedented escalation is a regime acting through institutional and ideological patterns laid down across two centuries: the bazaar-clergy alliance was forged in 1891-92; the trust deficit was laid in 1813-1907 and reinforced in 1953; Khomeini's 1970 Najaf lectures specified the IRGC-Basij architecture nine years *before* the 1979 revolution; the oil-and-state pattern was set by the 1901 D'Arcy Concession.

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

The 47-year-old Islamic Republic (1979-2026) is not the right analytical baseline for understanding Iran's behavior in the 2026 war. The relevant baseline runs back to **1813** (Treaty of Golestan, the first major Iranian territorial loss to Russia) and arguably to **1501** (Safavid imposition of Twelver Shi'ism as state religion). What looks in 2026 like an Iranian regime engaged in unprecedented escalation is in fact a regime acting through institutional and ideological patterns laid down across two centuries.

- The **bazaar-clergy alliance** that made the 1979 revolution and the 2026 IRGC-bonyad-clerical complex possible was forged in the 1891-92 Tobacco Protest.
- The **trust deficit** that makes US-Iran negotiation structurally suspect was laid in 1813-1907 (Russo-British Great Game), reinforced in 1953 (CIA-MI6 coup), and operationalized in 1979 (hostage crisis).
- The **velayat-e faqih** institutional design that produced today's IRGC dominance was articulated by Khomeini in nineteen Najaf lectures in **January-February 1970** — nine years before the revolution and 56 years before today.
- The **oil-and-state** pattern that locks Iran into resource-rentier politics was set by the 1901 D'Arcy Concession and the 1908 founding of APOC.

The Safavid-Islamic-Republic continuity is shallower than commonly assumed: the durable continuity is *Iran-as-Shi'i-state since 1501*, not *clerics-governing-the-state* (which is a 20th-century innovation). And the 1953 trust-deficit lineage is contested in the academic literature on causal weight, but its institutional weight in Iranian state ideology is real and load-bearing.

```{=html}
</div>
```

::: {.bottom-line}
**Bottom line.** Nine structural patterns laid down pre-1979 (with post-1979 institutional consolidation extending several into the contemporary form) shape what Iran does in 2026. They do not change the qualitative conclusions in the analytical chapters on this site — but they deepen several quantitatively, especially **Q1's trust deficit** (200 years, not 47), **Q2's regime-coalition depth** (the 50%+ parastatal economy crystallized in Rafsanjani's 1989-94 privatization stream capture, not in 1979), **Q6's reformist-failure base rate** (120 years, four sequential defeats, four-layer institutional defeat funnel), **Q10's oil-and-state genealogy** (1901 D'Arcy → 1954 IOP consortium → 2026), and **Q11's coalition prototype** (the 1953 Anglo-American intelligence team is the structural template for the 2026 US-Israel coalition).
:::

## Three thematic sub-pages

Three patterns get sufficient analytical leverage that they live on their own pages:

::: {.callout-note}
### [Theology and theocracy — the Khameneist project](theology.qmd)

How a 1970 Najaf doctrinal innovation became the 2026 IRGC-led regime, and why that regime is now a *post-2009 Khameneist project* analytically distinct from the Khomeinist revolution. Covers velayat-e faqih, the 1989 absolute-guardianship amendment, marja'iyat as the surviving Najaf-quietist alternative, the religious-reformist theologians (Kadivar, Shabestari, Eshkevari, Soroush, Mousavian) and how their alternatives were institutionally defeated 1999-2011, and Kamrava's 2023 succession forecast — which predicted IRGC consolidation three years before Feb 28 2026.

::: {.callout-note}
### [The reformist-failure base rate — 1905-2026](reformist-failure-base-rate.qmd)

Four sequential reformist defeats over 120 years — Constitutional Revolution (1905-11), Mosaddegh (1951-53), Khatami (1997-2005), Pezeshkian (2024-26) — defeated by the same composable institutional mechanism. Covers the Khatami case as the cleanest exposure of the [four-layer funnel]{.gloss data-gloss="four-layer-reformist-defeat"} (Guardian Council pre-electoral veto + post-electoral legislative veto + judicial repression + parastatal violence), the [Bani Sadr seven-step template]{.gloss data-gloss="bani-sadr-marginalization"} (1981) as the institutional ancestor, and how the defeat has now operated at the *theological-doctrinal* level (Kamrava: Kadivar 1999 imprisonment + 2011 firing; Eshkevari 2000 death sentence + defrocking; Shabestari 2006 forced retirement). Quantitative anchor: **5-15% base-rate probability** for reformist-led termination of the 2026 war.

**Most relevant to:** [Q6 — what ends the war](../analyses/q6-what-ends-the-war.qmd), with cross-links to Q1.3 (phased reading), Q5 (bargaining range), Q11 (Iran's re-engagement options exhausted).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### [The trust-deficit lineage — 1813-2026](trust-deficit.qmd)

The 200-year template Tehran applies to every Western negotiation: Treaty of Golestan (1813) → Anglo-Russian partition (1907) → Reza Shah's 1941 Anglo-Soviet deposition → 1953 CIA-MI6 coup → 1979 hostage crisis → 2018 JCPOA exit → 2026 strikes. Includes the **1953 Anglo-American coalition** (Roosevelt-Wilber-Schwarzkopf + Zaehner-Derbyshire-Rashidian) as the *structural prototype* for the 2026 US-Israel coalition — same two-intelligence-led-powers-as-one-team architecture, 73 years later, with roles inverted (Israel now the senior strategic partner).

**Most relevant to:** [Q1 — why bargaining failed](../analyses/q1-why-bargaining-failed.qmd), [Q3 — ceasefire instability](../analyses/q3-ceasefire-instability.qmd), [Q9 — Europe-US relationship](../analyses/q9-europe-us-relationship.qmd), [Q11 — US-Israel coalition](../analyses/q11-us-israel-coalition.qmd).
:::

## Five additional patterns (cited in specific analyses)

The other five patterns are cited within one or two analytical chapters and are summarized briefly here. Click through to the relevant analyses for application-specific detail.

### Bazaar-clergy alliance (1891 → 2026)

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

*Origin: Tobacco Protest 1891-92.* Naser al-Din Shah granted a tobacco monopoly to British concessionaire Major Talbot; ~25% of Iranians smoked. The likely-fabricated Shirazi fatwa cancelled the concession; women in the Shah's own harem obeyed it over the shah. The mechanic established: *clerical income depends on bazaar prosperity; bazaar mobilization depends on clerical sanction.* By 2026 the IRGC + bonyads + clerical complex controls ~50%+ of Iranian GDP outside the formal state — the template scaled into a parastatal complex. Crystallized into contemporary form in **Rafsanjani's 1989-94 privatization stream capture** (revolutionary-credentialed share-buyer rules delivered the privatization wave to bonyads, IRGC affiliates, and clerical-associated entities). Most relevant to [Q2 — war persistence](../analyses/q2-war-persistence.qmd) and [Q4 — counter-blockade feasibility](../analyses/q4-blockade-feasibility.qmd).

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

*Origin: Tobacco Protest 1891-92.* Naser al-Din Shah granted a tobacco monopoly to British concessionaire Major Talbot. ~25% of the Iranian population were regular tobacco smokers. The merchant guild head likely fabricated the Shirazi fatwa from Mirza Hasan Shirazi (the senior Shi'i marja). Women in the shah's own harem obeyed the fatwa over the shah's command. Concession cancelled — the first modern Iranian mass movement. *Established the mechanic: clerical income depends on bazaar prosperity; bazaar mobilization depends on clerical sanction.* This is the genetic origin point of every subsequent Iranian mass mobilization, including 1905-11, 1953, 1963, 1978-79.

*1979: The bazaar-clergy alliance fully operationalized.* 1960s Hay'atha-ye Mow'talefeh (bazaar-mosque coalition) built the network infrastructure. 1978 protest cycle ran on bazaar strikes + mosque mobilization + cassette tapes (a network template Khomeini pioneered with his 3 June 1963 Fayziyeh sermon). 1979 *komitehs* formalized the alliance as state structure. May 1979 IRGC formalization built the security counterpart. March 1979 Mostaz'afan Foundation absorbed all confiscated Pahlavi assets (became Iran's second-largest economic entity by 1989: 1,024 entities, $20B value).

*1989-94: Crystallization into the parastatal complex.* The 1989 Khomeini-to-Khamenei transition opened a Khamenei-Rafsanjani alliance that ran the post-Khomeini state. Rafsanjani's first five-year plan (1989-93) launched a market-reform program and an IMF-style structural adjustment. Privatization of more than a thousand state enterprises began in 1993 and was suspended a year later "largely because of widespread scandals and corruption." The Majles then passed legislation requiring privileged access for share-buyers "who had sacrificed for the revolution" — a mechanism by which the bonyads, IRGC affiliates, and clerical-associated entities captured the privatization stream. *This is the institutional event that produced the 50%+ GDP parastatal economy of 2026.* The Conoco embargo (April 1995) and the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act (1996) blocked the foreign capital and technology Rafsanjani's reforms required, deepening dependence on bonyad-mediated economic activity. *Any Iranian pragmatist who tries to integrate Iran with the global economy is sabotaged from inside (by the bonyad-bazaar coalition that profits from sanctions-driven scarcity rents) and from outside (by US sanctions enacted during precisely the attempted opening).* This pattern recurred under Khatami, Rouhani, and Pezeshkian.

*2026: The same template, vastly more capitalized.* The IRGC + bonyads + clerical complex now controls ~50%+ of Iranian GDP outside the formal state. Khatam al-Anbiya: 800+ subsidiaries, $25B in oil/gas contracts (2009-11 alone). Setad: $95-200B in holdings. Mostaz'afan: 350 subsidiaries. *The institutional template — bazaar-clergy alliance scaled into a parastatal complex — is older, deeper, and more replicable than IRGC org-charts suggest. Defeating the IRGC kinetically does not eliminate the template.*

</div>

### Oil-and-state pattern (1901 → 2026)

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

1901 **D'Arcy Concession**: 60-year monopoly granted tax-free for £40,000 + 16% of "net profit." Khuzestan struck 1908; APOC founded same year. Churchill's 1914 Admiralty purchase made the British *government* the concession holder. 1933 AIOC revision extended the concession to 1993. 1954 **IOP consortium** (BP 40%, Shell 14%, five US majors 8% each, CFP 6%) gave Iran the 50/50 deal AIOC had refused Mosaddegh. *The 2026 oil situation is the third act of a story whose first two acts were the 1901 D'Arcy Concession and the 1953 coup.* Today's renminbi-toll regime is the doctrinal break that lets Iran exit the dollar plumbing the IOP consortium imposed. Most relevant to [Q10 — US Hormuz interest](../analyses/q10-us-hormuz-interest.qmd).

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

*1901-1908: The original concession.* D'Arcy Concession (1901): 60-year monopoly granted tax-free for £40,000 + 16% of "net profit" (calculated by the concessionaire). Khuzestan struck 1908; APOC founded same year. Churchill's 1914 Admiralty purchase made the *British government* the concession holder.

*1924-1933: The Imbrie killing and AIOC revision.* 1924 Imbrie killing of the Sinclair concession by a mob in Tehran — eliminated US oil entry at the time. 1933 AIOC revision extended the concession to 1993 (60 more years).

*1951-1953: Mosaddegh's nationalization → 1953 coup.* Oil revenue: $45M (1950) → $905M (1969) — twentyfold nominal increase. Oil share of state revenue: 37% (1949-56) → 67% (1965). The 1954 IOP consortium gave Iran the 50/50 deal AIOC had refused Mosaddegh. *IOP composition: BP 40%, Royal Dutch Shell 14%, five US majors 8% each (Standard Oil of California / New Jersey / New York, Texaco, Gulf), CFP 6%.* This structure made Iran a definitively oil-rentier state.

*1979 → 2026.* 1979 nationalization completed what Mosaddegh started; APOC/AIOC/IOP heritage liquidated. 51% of FY2024-25 oil revenue went to armed forces — direct militarization. Today's renminbi-toll regime is the doctrinal break that lets Iran exit the dollar plumbing the IOP consortium imposed in 1954. *The 2026 oil situation is the third act of a story whose first two acts were the 1901 D'Arcy Concession and the 1953 coup.*

</div>

### Pahlavi-IRGC state-building parallels (1925 → 2026)

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

Despite ideological opposition, the Pahlavi state (1925-1979) and the Islamic Republic (1979-2026) are structurally similar in important ways: both are authoritarian-modernizing regimes centered on a single charismatic figure, sustained by a parallel security apparatus (Cossack-derived army → SAVAK → IRGC), funded by oil rentier income, engaged in massive infrastructure and social-engineering projects, and hostile to traditional political pluralism. **The IRGC didn't invent state-centralization; it inherited it from 50 years of Pahlavi state-building.** This is another argument for the *phased/structural* reading of 2026 — the institutional architecture was prepared decades before Khomeini's return. Most relevant to [Q1 — why bargaining failed](../analyses/q1-why-bargaining-failed.qmd) (Q1.3 phased reading) and [Q2 — war persistence](../analyses/q2-war-persistence.qmd).

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

The Pahlavi state (1925-1979) and the Islamic Republic (1979-2026) appear ideologically opposite but are structurally similar in important ways. Both are: authoritarian-modernizing regimes; centered on a single charismatic figure (Reza Shah → Mohammad Reza → Khomeini → Khamenei); sustained by a parallel security apparatus (Reza Shah's Cossack-derived army → SAVAK → IRGC); funded by oil rentier income; engaged in massive infrastructure and social-engineering projects; hostile to traditional political pluralism.

*Reza Shah's specifics (1925-1941).* Public schools grew 50× and education budget 200× between 1921-41. Literacy from 5% to 15%. Trans-Iranian Railroad cost ~$500M (most expensive Iranian project ever). Tehran population to 500,000 by 1941. Oil royalties = 25% of state revenue by 1940. 1936 unveiling decree (forced de-veiling of women).

*Mohammad Reza's specifics (1953-1979).* 1963 White Revolution: land reform, women's suffrage, literacy corps. Annual budget: $1B (1965) → $8B (1971) → $48B (1977) — 48-fold. 1973-74 oil shock: $1.95/bbl → ~$11/bbl. 1975 Rastakhiz Party (one-party system). Iran was a net food importer by early 1970s. 1977 Carter human-rights pressure → selective liberalization → revolution.

*The IRGC inversion (1979-2026).* Same authoritarian-modernizing template, *inverted into clerical-modernizing form*. Replaces Pahlavi monarchical legitimacy with *velayat-e faqih* religious legitimacy. Replaces SAVAK with IRGC + Basij + Ministry of Intelligence. Replaces Pahlavi-era foreign-direct-investment with bonyad-IRGC parastatal complex. *The structural template is the same; the ideological framing is opposite. This explains why the Islamic Republic could absorb and operationalize Pahlavi institutional infrastructure (military, civil service, oil sector) so quickly.*

```{=html}
</div>
```

### Pre-1979 regional positioning (1953 → 2026)

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

*Pre-1979 (1953-1979): Iran as US-aligned regional gendarme.* Periphery Doctrine: tacit Iran-Israel-Turkey alignment vs Arab nationalist threats. 1971 Pahlavi annexation of Abu Musa, Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb (still UAE territorial dispute today). 1973-1975 Dhofar intervention on behalf of Oman against PFLO insurgency. 1975 Algiers Accord: Iran-Iraq border resolved on terms humiliating to Iraq (Saddam tore this up to start the 1980 war). US-supplied AWACS, F-14s, F-4s; Iran was the largest US arms customer in the world by mid-1970s. *Iran was the Persian Gulf's hegemonic guarantor on US/Israeli terms.* **The 47-year inversion of this reality is the conceptual baseline** against which today's GCC behavior — accept some Iran-containment costs but not all — must be read. Most relevant to [Q12.4 — Gulf paradox](../analyses/q12-4-gulf-paradox.qmd) and [Q12.5 — post-war reconfiguration](../analyses/q12-5-post-war-reconfiguration.qmd).

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

*Pre-1979 (1953-1979): Iran as US-aligned regional gendarme.* Periphery Doctrine: tacit Iran-Israel-Turkey alignment vs Arab nationalist threats. 1971: Pahlavi annexation of Abu Musa, Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb (still UAE territorial dispute today). 1973-1975: Dhofar intervention on behalf of Oman against PFLO insurgency. 1975 Algiers Accord: Iran-Iraq border resolved on terms humiliating to Iraq (Saddam tore this up to start the 1980 war). US-supplied AWACS, F-14s, F-4s; Iran was the largest US arms customer in the world by mid-1970s. Israel: oil supply through Eilat-Ashkelon pipeline; intelligence cooperation. *Iran was the Persian Gulf's hegemonic guarantor on US/Israeli terms.*

*1979 inversion → 2026 endpoint.* 1979 revolution: Iran exits the US security architecture. Hostage crisis ends Iran-US relations. Israel switches from Pahlavi-ally to existential adversary of revolutionary Iran. 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war: GCC backs Saddam; Iran isolated regionally. 2003 Iraq war removes Saddam (Iran's adversary) — opens pathway for Iran's regional reach via Iraqi Shia networks. 2011 Syria civil war: Iran backs Assad; Saudi backs Sunni opposition. 2015 JCPOA: temporary Iran-US thaw, GCC anxious. 2019 Abqaiq attack (5.7 mb/d disrupted) + Trump non-retaliation: Saudi internalizes US guarantee has limits. 2023 China-brokered Saudi-Iran rapprochement: GCC hedges. 2026 war: Saudi/UAE publicly support strikes but decline operational role; rapprochement in suspended animation.

**The 47-year arc.** Iran went from US gendarme → US adversary → regional power → bracketed power. The GCC went from threatened-by-Iran-and-protected-by-US → threatened-by-Iran-but-uncertain-about-US-protection → hedging-between-Iran-and-US-and-China. *The pre-1979 Iran-as-Gulf-gendarme reality is the conceptual baseline against which today's GCC behavior — accept some Iran-containment costs but not all — must be read.*

### The 1953 coalition as 2026 prototype (treated under [Trust deficit](trust-deficit.qmd))

The 1953 operational team — Roosevelt-Wilber-Schwarzkopf (US) + Zaehner-Derbyshire-Rashidian (UK) — is the *structural prototype* for the 2026 US-Israel coalition. *Two intelligence-led powers operating as one covert team*, with the senior-junior dynamic now inverted (Israel = senior strategic partner with Octopus Doctrine; US = junior follower with greater operational resources). The 1953 coup was officially acknowledged by the CIA in 2013 and formally taken credit for in 2023 — meaning the *prototype* itself is now part of the public-domain US-side institutional memory in a way it was not when JCPOA was signed. Detailed on the [Trust deficit](trust-deficit.qmd) page; most relevant to [Q11 — US-Israel coalition](../analyses/q11-us-israel-coalition.qmd).

Tehran applies the Truman → Eisenhower (1951-53) template to every US admin transition; JCPOA (2015-18) maps onto this template directly. The 1979 constitutional architecture the IRGC inherited is itself a procedurally captured outcome — Bazargan's PRG draft displaced by an August 1979 Khomeinist-controlled Assembly of Experts under boycott conditions — so the IRGC veto is built on a captured institutional baseline, not a popular mandate. See [Trust deficit](trust-deficit.qmd). |

## Sources & further reading

This page synthesizes the project's pre-1979 historical corpus, which has three layers.

**Pre-1979 Amanat corpus (the patterns through 1989).** Abbas Amanat's *Iran: A Modern History* (Yale, 2017) is the principal anchor, supplemented by Stephen Kinzer's *All the Shah's Men* (2003), Roy Mottahedeh's *Mantle of the Prophet* (1985), Said Amir Arjomand's *The Turban for the Crown* (1988), Misagh Parsa's *Social Origins of the Iranian Revolution* (1989), Charles Kurzman's *The Unthinkable Revolution* (2004), Ervand Abrahamian's *Iran Between Two Revolutions* (1982) and *History of Modern Iran* (2008), Khomeini's 1970 Najaf lectures (*Hokumat-e Islami*), the Wilber CIA history, and Gasiorowski's TPBEDAMN documentation.

**Post-1979 political-sociological consolidation (1989-2006).** Amanat's narrative ends ~1989. The post-1989 institutional-consolidation material — Bani Sadr template, Rafsanjani's 1989-94 parastatal crystallization, the Khatami-era four-layer reformist defeat, the November 2005 Russian nuclear compromise rejection, and the Najaf quietist tradition (Borujerdi → Khoei → Sistani) as institutional alternative to velayat-e faqih — draws on Nikki R. Keddie, *Modern Iran: Roots and Results of Revolution* (Yale 2003, updated edition with 2006 Epilogue), with Yann Richard's "Contemporary Shi'i Thought" chapter providing the canonical English-language treatment of 20th-century Shi'i political theology.

**Theological-jurisprudential dimension (through ~2023).** Mehran Kamrava, *How Islam Rules in Iran: Theology and Theocracy in the Islamic Republic* (Cambridge 2024). Kamrava (Director of the Iranian Studies Unit at the Arab Center for Research and Policy Studies in Doha; Professor of Government at Georgetown University in Qatar) brings Persian-language sources — Iranian academic publications, clerical memoirs, Qom seminary publications — into English translation for the first time. The book's distinctive analytical contributions: dissecting "Khameneism" as a distinct ideological project; the post-Khomeini decoupling of marja'iyat from velayat-e faqih; the theological substance of the 1990s reformist intellectual project and the *mechanism* of its institutional defeat; the forward-looking 2023 succession scenario analysis.

All are public published works; the synthesis here is original. The three sources are analytically complementary: Amanat is cultural-literary; Keddie is political-sociological; Kamrava is theological-jurisprudential. Together they span 20th- and early-21st-century Iranian institutional development relevant to the 2026 war.
